For mean logistic loss, the smooth gradient is Xᵀ(sigmoid(Xw+b)−y)/N plus lambda2·w. Take that gradient step, then soft-threshold each weight by learning_rate·lambda1. The proximal step creates exact zeros; adding sign(w) to a gradient is not ISTA. The intercept remains unpenalized. Features and step size control convergence.

**Mathematical and practical explanation.** The proximal map for an L1 term is $\operatorname{soft}(v,a)=\operatorname{sign}(v)\max(|v|-a,0)$. Apply it to $v=w-\eta\nabla L_{smooth}$ with $a=\eta\lambda_1$. This explicitly solves the local nonsmooth subproblem and produces exact zeros; a sign-gradient step can cross zero repeatedly without creating the same sparse solution. [3](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/linear_model.html)
